tasks.title: Define the internal readiness package
tasks.description: Create one canonical internal readiness package covering scan freshness, staging proof, compatibility proof, rollback proof, release evidence, and explicit deferral of external audit for this cycle.
acceptance_criteria: One internal readiness package covers the required evidence families.
Evidence freshness rules are explicit.
External audit is documented as deferred for this cycle.
test_cases: Run the UW validator and verify all planning artifacts reference the same internal gate.
Review readiness docs and confirm no task depends on external audit completion.
tasks.expected_output: Internal readiness gate definition and evidence contract
definition_of_done: Internal gate is explicit across all UW artifacts.
Freshness expectations are documented.
Later work can depend on the gate without ambiguity.

tier.justification: Low-ambiguity planning and gating task with high leverage.

tasks.title: Remove tracked artifact noise and define hygiene expectations
tasks.description: Clean tracked __pycache__, .pyc, and temporary artifact noise from the repo state, then define ignore and hygiene expectations so the noise does not return.
acceptance_criteria: Tracked artifact noise is removed.
Prevention guidance or ignore rules are updated.
The cleanup scope is reflected in the internal readiness package.
test_cases: Check git status and repo state after cleanup.
Verify hygiene rules cover the removed artifact families.
tasks.expected_output: Cleaner repo state with explicit hygiene rules
definition_of_done: Tracked noise is removed.
Hygiene expectations are documented.
No active task depends on stale artifact files.

tier.justification: Straightforward cleanup task with immediate credibility payoff.

tasks.title: Publish one canonical CI and release workflow map
tasks.description: Inventory overlapping CI and deploy workflows, identify the canonical release path, and categorize duplicates as legacy or deprecation candidates.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical CI and release workflow map exists.
Duplicate or ambiguous workflow files are identified clearly.
The internal readiness package references the same canonical workflow set.
test_cases: Cross-check the map against .github/workflows.
Verify readiness docs reference the same canonical workflow set.
tasks.expected_output: Canonical CI and release workflow map
definition_of_done: Canonical workflows are documented.
Ambiguous duplicates are categorized.
Release readiness references one clear workflow path.

tier.justification: Moderate repo-wide planning and curation task.

tasks.title: Reconcile security docs with the current operational state
tasks.description: Update security-facing docs and checklists so they reflect the actual current state around rate limiting, key rotation, alerts, and the internal-readiness scope.
acceptance_criteria: Security checklist statements match the real current state.
Internal-readiness language does not imply external-audit closure.
Security-specific alert expectations are explicit.
test_cases: Review docs/SECURITY.md against implemented controls and known gaps.
Verify the internal readiness package and security docs do not contradict each other.
tasks.expected_output: Security docs aligned to the current cycle scope
definition_of_done: Security docs are internally consistent.
Known gaps are explicit instead of implied resolved.
The internal gate can cite the docs without contradiction.

tier.justification: Docs-alignment task with moderate risk if left inconsistent.

tasks.title: Define explicit production and fallback semantics for the workflow engine
tasks.description: Audit workflow_engine.rs, define what production mode means, and make fallback behavior explicit when Temporal is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Production and fallback semantics are explicit.
Transitional Temporal request behavior is identified and scoped.
Operators can explain runtime behavior during Temporal unavailability.
test_cases: Review workflow-engine code paths against the documented contract.
Verify product spec and implementation plan use the same runtime terminology.
tasks.expected_output: Documented workflow runtime contract
definition_of_done: Operators and engineers can explain the runtime contract.
The contract is reflected in UW artifacts.
Follow-on tasks can test the chosen behavior.

tier.justification: High-impact runtime hardening task with meaningful correctness risk.

tasks.title: Add tests for the chosen workflow runtime contract
tasks.description: Add or tighten targeted tests so the chosen production and fallback semantics for the workflow engine are enforced and regressions are caught early.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover the agreed production and fallback behavior.
The tests fail meaningfully if transitional behavior regresses.
The internal readiness slice can cite runtime tests as evidence.
test_cases: Run targeted workflow-engine tests for fallback and production behavior.
Run cargo check or targeted test commands for affected crates.
tasks.expected_output: Test-backed workflow runtime contract
definition_of_done: Runtime contract tests exist and pass.
The test surface is referenced by the readiness gate.
Future changes can rely on the tests for regressions.

tier.justification: Focused hardening task with moderate scope and clear payoff.

tasks.title: Add security-specific operational alerting
tasks.description: Add security-oriented alerts such as brute-force or unusual auth or key abuse patterns and align their coverage with the security checklist and release-readiness expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Security-oriented alerts are defined.
Reliability and security alert classes are distinguished.
Security docs reflect the alert coverage accurately.
test_cases: Review alert rules and monitoring coverage.
Verify docs and internal gate references align with the alert definitions.
tasks.expected_output: Security alerting slice aligned with internal-readiness needs
definition_of_done: Security-specific alert coverage exists.
Docs and monitoring definitions are aligned.
Operators can distinguish reliability from security alerting.

tier.justification: Operational hardening task bridging monitoring and docs.

tasks.title: Define the treasury live-evidence seam and provenance model
tasks.description: Design or extend the treasury read seam so imported evidence and provenance become first-class inputs to the treasury workbench instead of sample-heavy defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Treasury evidence and provenance are first-class concepts.
Sample-only defaults are removed or explicitly labeled.
The design remains additive to current treasury services and handlers.
test_cases: Review treasury service code and current sample-heavy behavior.
Verify provenance fields are represented in planning artifacts.
tasks.expected_output: Treasury live-evidence seam and provenance model
definition_of_done: Treasury data model references live evidence and provenance.
The operator default path can move off synthetic state.
The design does not fork the treasury control plane.

tier.justification: High-value operator truth task with moderate modeling ambiguity.

tasks.title: Wire treasury workbench defaults to evidence-backed reads
tasks.description: Implement the first treasury workbench slice that reads from live evidence and exposes provenance on the current admin surface and exports.
acceptance_criteria: Treasury workbench defaults to evidence-backed reads.
Provenance is visible in operator output or export metadata.
Current admin shell shape is preserved.
test_cases: Run treasury service and handler tests for evidence-backed behavior.
Verify export paths still function with provenance metadata.
tasks.expected_output: Evidence-backed treasury workbench default path
definition_of_done: Treasury default reads are evidence-backed.
Provenance is surfaced to operators.
Exports remain compatible.

tier.justification: Cross-layer task affecting service, admin, and export surfaces.

tasks.title: Define reconciliation evidence lineage and live-read model
tasks.description: Add reconciliation evidence, discrepancy lineage, and workflow linkage as first-class concepts so the synthetic default path can be retired.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation evidence and lineage are first-class concepts.
Default reads do not depend on synthetic-only state.
The design stays additive to current reconciliation seams.
test_cases: Review reconciliation services and current synthetic behavior.
Verify lineage fields are represented in planning artifacts.
tasks.expected_output: Reconciliation evidence lineage and live-read model
definition_of_done: Reconciliation lineage is part of the data model.
Synthetic defaults can be retired.
The design remains additive.

tier.justification: Critical operator-truth modeling task with multiple downstream consumers.

tasks.title: Wire reconciliation workbench defaults to evidence-backed reads
tasks.description: Implement the first reconciliation workbench slice that reads from evidence and lineage while keeping mutate actions operator-assisted and attributable.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation views show evidence and lineage.
Default reads are not synthetic-only.
Mutate actions remain operator-assisted and attributable.
test_cases: Run reconciliation service and handler tests against lineage-backed reads.
Verify discrepancy views can reference evidence sources.
tasks.expected_output: Evidence-backed reconciliation workbench default path
definition_of_done: Reconciliation default reads are live-backed.
Lineage is visible to operators.
The existing admin shell remains intact.

tasks.title: Audit CLI coverage truth against the ledger
tasks.description: Compare implemented CLI command families against docs/cli/coverage-ledger.md, classify unsupported READY items, and make the coverage contract honest.
acceptance_criteria: CLI coverage truth is audited against the ledger.
READY claims are honest.

Verify docs and parser help stay in sync during the audit.
tasks.expected_output: CLI coverage truth audit
definition_of_done: Coverage claims are honest.

tasks.title: Close the READY-surface parity gap in the packaged CLI
tasks.description: Implement or reclassify READY ledger items so the packaged CLI, docs, and backend surface agree on what is truly supported.
acceptance_criteria: READY ledger items are implemented or reclassified honestly.
Parser behavior, docs, and smoke tests agree.

test_cases: Run CLI parser tests and smoke tests.
Cross-check implemented command families against the updated ledger.
tasks.expected_output: Truthful CLI parity for READY surfaces
definition_of_done: CLI parity gap is materially smaller.
Coverage claims are honest.
Smoke tests reflect the real supported surface.

tier.justification: Core agent-surface task with moderate breadth and manageable risk.

tasks.title: Replace or remove placeholder CLI command behavior
tasks.description: Eliminate placeholder command behavior such as sandbox run by backing it with real backend behavior or removing it from the supported CLI surface.
acceptance_criteria: Placeholder command behavior is gone from the supported surface.
Any bounded command is clearly labeled as such.
CLI docs reflect the real supported behavior.
test_cases: Run CLI smoke tests for the affected commands.
Verify parser help no longer implies unsupported behavior.
tasks.expected_output: Placeholder-free supported CLI surface
definition_of_done: Placeholder behavior is removed or replaced.
Docs match the parser.
The supported CLI surface is truthful.

tasks.title: Add one JSONL watch flow for a real operational stream
tasks.description: Implement one real JSONL watch mode for an operational stream using existing websocket or event seams and document the stable output schema for agent use.
acceptance_criteria: At least one real stream emits stable JSONL.
The stream reuses existing event or websocket seams.
The output schema is documented and testable.

tasks.expected_output: First real JSONL watch flow for agent consumption
definition_of_done: A real JSONL stream exists.
The output schema is stable enough for agent use.
The watch path is part of the supported CLI surface.

tasks.title: Add approval-aware boundaries for side-effecting CLI commands
tasks.description: Classify high-risk mutate commands separately from read-only flows and define explicit approval or confirmation semantics for dangerous operator actions.
acceptance_criteria: High-risk mutate commands have explicit approval or confirmation boundaries.

Verify dangerous commands have explicit approval or confirmation behavior.
tasks.expected_output: Approval-aware mutate command contract
definition_of_done: Read and write command classes are explicit.
High-risk mutate flows cannot be mistaken for read-only automation.
Approval semantics are documented in the CLI surface.

tasks.title: Draft an MCP-ready contract for the first operator-safe tool surfaces

Verify input and output schema expectations are explicit.
tasks.expected_output: MCP-ready tool contract draft for first operator-safe surfaces

Input and output schema expectations are documented.
The draft can guide a later implementation slice.

tasks.title: Design registry-backed config bundle and extension governance

Verify secret and approval assumptions are explicit and additive.

Secrets remain indirect.
